title: Reserve Shares Kept Back From a Draw on a Keyturn Host Payout Account
content:
The share of the drawable sum on a Keyturn Host Payout Account kept back as routine reserve turns on how many trips the account has been credited for and on whether it is still carrying reserves.

**Where fewer than 10 trip earnings, being the schedule's qualifying number, have been credited to the account in the twelve months up to that day**, the new-host reserve share of 10 percent applies.

**Where 10 trip earnings or more have been credited to it in that period and a reserve has been taken on the account in that period**, the routine reserve share of 3 percent applies.

**In every other case**, no reserve share is kept back from the drawable sum, the share standing at 0 percent.

The share is taken on the payable balance, and the sum kept back is rounded half to even to two decimal places.

## The count, from both sides

The count runs on trip earnings credited to the account in the twelve months up to that day, one to an entry. At 9 such entries the first case governs at 10 percent; at 10 the first case no longer governs, and the account falls to the second or the third according to whether a reserve has been taken on it in that same period.

## The second test

An account credited for 10 trip earnings or more in that period on which no reserve has been taken in that period meets neither of the first two cases, so the third governs and nothing is kept back.

## On hypothetical figures

Where the payable balance is 4000.00 USD, the sum kept back is 400.00 USD in the first case, 120.00 USD in the second and 0.00 USD in the third.
